column2: Have you investigated the impact of elements like glasses or masks on the Sharpness Algorithm? I'm particularly curious whether strong borders, such as those from eyeglass frames, might influence the results.
column6:
The Occlusion SEgmentation CNN used by OFIQ considers frames of glasses as occlusions. Thus, the occlusion of eyes and the face are reflected in the ouputs of the algoruthms for Face Occlusion Prevention and Eyes Visible. 
The impact of glasses to the outputs of the Sharpness algoruthm have not (yet) been investigated. This might be analyzed in the development of OFIQ 2.0. 
Another issue with glasses are distortions of the eye region (in case of strong lenses), but also reflections on the glasses. Both issues are difficult to detect (I doubt, there is an algorithm able to detect such distrtions accurately), but we will further look for eligible algorithms. Any suggestions are welcome!

column2: It is acknowledged that, akin to fingerprints, the anatomy of the ear is unique. To this end, what algorithm has been implemented to facilitate lobular or pinna recognition? column2: Is there any focus on transaction speed for upcoming releases (the base existing version is quite slow).

We have already identified very promising landmark estimation models that achieve a comarable accuraacy at only 40% of the exeution time. The same holds for face parsing the second most time consuming step. For use cases, where checking Background Uniformity  and Head Coverings is not necessrary, the Face Parsing will be skipped alltogether.

column2: Based on the observations of FNMR vs Fraction of rejected genuine could you share the top 3 or top 5 factors with the highest impact after Unified Quality score?
column6:
We haven't analysized this explicitly. However, we have computed EDC curves for almost all OFIQ algorithms. Algorithms, whose outputs correlate strongly with match screws show a stong decline of FNMR in the corresponding EDC. Some algorithms  show very little, no or even negative correlation. This doesn't mean that the algorithms are bad, but it yould be that the quality aspect checked has litte / no / negative impact on face recognition. for instance, the EDC curve of the OFIQ algorithm for Expression Neutrality shows no decline of the FNMR, and we believe that this is due to the fact that 
a) the by far the most frequent facial expression in the test set (VGGFace2) is Smiling and   
b) modern face recognition algorithms are trained on such images and are, thus, not negatively affected by a smile.
But actually, we not analyzed the impact of the ground truth quality aspects on the performance of face recognition algorithms. this qould require large data sets with ground truth labels.

column2: Based on the observations of FNMR vs Fraction of rejected genuine could you share the top 3 or top 5 factors with the highest impact after Unified Quality score?
column6: I would say that the face / eye / mouth occlusion algorithms along with head pose (yaw and pitch) have the strongest correlation. Small inter-eye distance also has a great impact but not for values over 70 (face regognition algorithms typically take as input face crops of 112x112 pixels only). Sharpness and compression can also have a large impact but only in cases where these defects are still visible on the small face crops used as input.
